=== WHY I HAD TO REPLACE IT RATHER THAN ADD ALONGSIDE — A GATE DEFECT I FOUND WHILE DOING IT ===
scripts/lwb_lanes.py fails the gate on ANY non-conforming record in reviews/<pr>/, including a
DISAGREE, even when the required number of valid AGREEs is also present. Measured: I put a
well-formed AGREE record naming the reviewable head into reviews/39/ ALONGSIDE my DISAGREE and ran
    python scripts/lwb_lanes.py --base origin/main --head HEAD --pr-number 39
  -> EXIT 1, and the only failure was "reviews/39/cloud-reviewer-b.json: verdict is 'DISAGREE',
     want 'AGREE'".
The cause is structural, not incidental: independent_reviews() calls _review_ok() on every record
and _review_ok appends to the shared `errors` list for each one that does not conform, while the CLI
fails whenever `errors` is non-empty. So reviews/<pr>/ is append-only in effect, and ONE DISAGREE
blocks its PR permanently — the gate cannot be satisfied afterwards by any amount of fixing, only by
editing or deleting that record.
CONSEQUENCE WORTH AN OWNER'S ATTENTION, measured in the same run: PR #29 carries eight DISAGREE
records and PR #32 carries six. Even if every substantive finding on those branches were fixed
tomorrow, lwb-lanes would still be red, for the records alone. Two of those records are mine, filed
today; I am naming a problem I am part of, not one I only observed.
A reviewer that DISAGREEs is therefore on the hook to come back and update its own record, which is
what I am doing here, and which nothing in reviews/README.md currently says.
